subfields.name: Universal Id
subfields.description: The HDs second component, <universal ID> (UID), is a string formatted according to the scheme defined by the third component, <universal ID type> (UID type). The UID is intended to be unique over time within the UID type. It is rigorously defined. Each UID must belong to one of the specifically enumerated schemes for constructing UIDs (defined by the UID type). The UID (second component) must follow the syntactic rules of the particular universal identifier scheme (defined by the third component). Note that these syntactic rules are not defined within HL7 but are defined by the rules of the particular universal identifier scheme (defined by the third component).

subfields.name: Universal Id Type
subfields.description: The third component governs the interpretation of the second component of the HD. If the third component is a known UID refer to HL7 Table 0301 - Universal ID type for valid values, then the second component is a universal ID of that type.

subfields.name: Family Name
subfields.description: This component allows full specification of the surname of a person. Where appropriate, it differentiates the person's own surname from that of the person's partner or spouse, in cases where the person's name may contain elements from either name. It also permits messages to distinguish the surname prefix (such as "van" or "de") from the surname root. See section 2.A.30, "FN - family name".

subfields.name: Professional Suffix
subfields.description: Used to specify an abbreviation, or a string of abbreviations denoting qualifications that support the persons profession, (e.g., licenses, certificates, degrees, affiliations with professional societies, etc.). The Professional Suffix normally follows the Family Name when the Person Name is used for display purposes. Please note that this component is an unformatted string and is used for display purposes only. Detailed information regarding the contents of Professional Suffix is obtained using appropriate segments in Chapter 15, Personnel Management.

Indicates the degree of precision of the time stamp (Y = year, L = month, D = day, H = hour, M = minute, S = second). Refer to HL7 Table 0529 - Precision for valid value.

subfields.name: Id Number
subfields.description: The value of the identifier itself.

subfields.name: Assigning Agency Or Department
subfields.description: The agency or department that assigned the identifier in component 1.

subfields.name: Check Digit
subfields.description: The check digit in this data type is not an add-on produced by the message processor. It is the check digit that is part of the identifying number used in the sending application. If the sending application does not include a self-generated check digit in the identifying number, this component should be valued null.

subfields.name: Check Digit Scheme
subfields.description: Contains the code identifying the check digit scheme employed.

subfields.name: Assigning Authority
subfields.description: The assigning authority is a unique name of the system (or organization or agency or department) that creates the data. . Refer to User-defined Table 0363 - Assigning authority for suggested values.

subfields.name: Identifier Type Code
subfields.description: A code corresponding to the type of identifier. In some cases, this code may be used as a qualifier to the Assigning authority component. Refer to HL7 Table 0203 - Identifier type for suggested values.

subfields.name: Assigning Facility
subfields.description: The place or location identifier where the identifier was first assigned to the patient. This component is not an inherent part of the identifier but rather part of the history of the identifier: as part of this data type, its existence is a convenience for certain intercommunicating systems.

subfields.name: Effective Date
subfields.description: The first date, if known, on which the identifier is valid and active.

subfields.name: Expiration Date
subfields.description: The last date, if known, on which the identifier is valid and active.

subfields.name: Assigning Jurisdiction
subfields.description: The geo-political body that assigned the identifier in component 1.

subfields.name: Id Number
subfields.description: This string refers to the coded ID according to a user-defined table, defined by the 9th component. If the first component is present, either the source table or the assigning authority must be valued.

subfields.name: Name Type Code
subfields.description: A code that represents the type of name. Refer to HL7 Table 0200 - Name type for valid values. See Section 2.A.88.7, " Name Type Code (ID) ".

subfields.name: Identifier Check Digit
subfields.description: The check digit in this data type is not an add-on produced by the message processor. It is the check digit that is part of the identifying number used in the sending application. If the sending application does not include a self-generated check digit in the identifying number, this component should be valued null.

subfields.name: Check Digit Scheme
subfields.description: Contains the code identifying the check digit scheme employed.

subfields.name: Identifier Type Code
subfields.description: A code corresponding to the type of identifier. In some cases, this code may be used as a qualifier to the <assigning authority> component. Refer to HL7 Table 0203 - Identifier type for suggested values.

subfields.name: Assigning Facility
subfields.description: The place or location identifier where the identifier was first assigned to the person. This component is not an inherent part of the identifier but rather part of the history of the identifier: as part of this data type, its existence is a convenience for certain intercommunicating systems.

subfields.name: Name Representation Code
subfields.description: Different <name/address types> and representations of the same <name/address> should be described by repeating of this field, with different values of the <name/address type> and/or <name/address representation> component.

subfields.name: Name Context
subfields.description: This component is used to designate the context in which a name is used. The main use case is in Australian healthcare for indigenous patients who prefer to use different names when attending different healthcare institutions. Another use case occurs in the US where health practitioners can be licensed under slightly different names and the reporting of the correct name is vital for administrative purposes. Refer to User-defined Table 0448 - Name context for suggested values.

subfields.name: Name Validity Range
subfields.description:
Retained for backward compatibility only as of v 2.5. Refer to XCN.19 Effective Date and XCN.20 Expiration Date instead. This component cannot be fully expressed and has been identified as v 2.4 erratum.

This component contains the start and end date/times that define the period during which this name was valid. See section 2.A.20, " DR - date/time range " for description of subcomponents.

subfields.name: Name Assembly Order
subfields.description: A code that represents the preferred display order of the components of this person name. Refer to HL7 Table 0444 - Name Assembly Order for valid values.

subfields.name: Effective Date
subfields.description: The first date, if known, on which the address is valid and active.

subfields.name: Family Name
subfields.description: This component allows full specification of the surname of a person. Where appropriate, it differentiates the person's own surname from that of the person's partner or spouse, in cases where the person's name may contain elements from either name. It also permits messages to distinguish the surname prefix (such as "van" or "de") from the surname root. See section 2.A.30, " FN - family name".

subfields.name: Expiration Date
subfields.description: The last date, if known, on which the address is valid and active.

subfields.name: Professional Suffix
subfields.description: Used to specify an abbreviation, or a string of abbreviations denoting qualifications that support the persons profession, (e.g., licenses, certificates, degrees, affiliations with professional societies, etc.). The Professional Suffix normally follows the Family Name when the Person Name is used for display purposes. Please note that this component is an unformatted string and is used for display purposes only. Detailed information regarding the contents of Professional Suffix is obtained using appropriate segments in Chapter 15, Personnel Management.

subfields.name: Assigning Jurisdiction
subfields.description: The geo-political body that assigned the identifier in component 1.

subfields.name: Assigning Agency Or Department
subfields.description: The agency or department that assigned the identifier in component 1.

subfields.name: Given Name
subfields.description: First name.

subfields.name: Second And Further Given Names Or Initials Thereof
subfields.description: Multiple middle names may be included by separating them with spaces.

subfields.name: Suffix (e.g., Jr Or Iii)
subfields.description: Used to specify a name suffix (e.g., Jr. or III).

subfields.name: Prefix (e.g., Dr)
subfields.description: Used to specify a name prefix (e.g., Dr.).

subfields.name: Degree (e.g., Md)
subfields.description: Retained for backward compatibility only as of v 2.5. See Professional Suffix component.

subfields.name: Source Table
subfields.description: CN ID source is used as the HL7 identifier for the user-defined table of values for this component. Used to delineate the first component.

subfields.name: Assigning Authority
subfields.description: The assigning authority is a unique identifier of the system (or organization or agency of department) that creates the data. User-defined Table 0363 - Assigning authority is used as the HL7 identifier for the user-defined table of values for the first sub-component of the HD component, <namespace ID>.
